Winery

Bodega Colomé

Historic winery in the Calchaquí Valleys of Salta, whose origins go back to 1831. It is known for its very high-altitude vineyards, among the highest in the world.

Colomé lies in an isolated valley in the department of Molinos, in the upper part of the Calchaquí Valleys, and is considered one of the oldest working wineries in Argentina, with origins in 1831. During the nineteenth century the estate belonged to figures linked to the history of Salta, and some of its old ungrafted vines are still in production.

In 2001 the property was acquired by the Swiss businessman Donald Hess, owner of wineries in California and other countries, who renovated the winery, restored the old vineyards and planted new ones at extraordinary altitudes. Notable among them is the Altura Máxima estate, located more than 3,000 metres above sea level and considered one of the highest vineyards in the world. Today the winery is part of the Hess family’s wine group.

The high altitude exposes the grapes to very intense sunlight and to wide temperature differences between day and night, which results in deeply coloured, highly concentrated wines, especially from Malbec, and aromatic Torrontés whites. The estate practises environmentally conscious viticulture and has a small hotel and a museum devoted to the work of the American artist James Turrell, known for his light installations. The journey to Colomé, along mountain roads, is part of the experience of a visit.

Visits & wine tourism

The estate has a hotel, a restaurant and the James Turrell museum, and offers tours and tastings; given its remote location it is advisable to check before travelling.
